analysis.title: Weekly Viewpoint: Risk-Off Sentiment Pushes S&P Into a Technical Correction
key_insights: Week ending 11/20: Dow -8.0%, S&P 500 -8.6%, Nasdaq -10.0%. All 11 S&P sectors fell, with tech (-12.2%) weakest, then communication services (-9.4%) and materials (-7.9%).
S&P 500 extended its losing streak to seven sessions and entered a technical correction, a 10% pullback from its all-time high. The selloff was global.

AI trade anxiety persisted despite strong Nvidia results and guidance and a successful Anthropic public offering. Added pressure came from increased risk of US strikes on Iran and growing risk of hacks and system outages.
Fed speak leaned hawkish. Waller said the Fed should raise 50bp in December if it will not signal a more aggressive pace, as he worries people see 3% inflation as the new norm.

Jefferson and Goolsbee said the AI buildout is putting upward pressure on inflation and risks overheating the economy. Goolsbee will consider a larger than usual hike. Kashkari flagged concentration risk if AI investment underdelivers.
Williams dismissed the need for an outsized hike but said more work remains on inflation. Musalem backed multiple hikes in coming months.

Minutes of the Oct 27-28 FOMC showed nearly all officials expect to raise rates in the months ahead. Two said more than 25bp could be warranted in December if inflation data is unfavorable. The hold was a close call for a few.
Q3 earnings: 468 S&P 500 companies have reported, with over 84% beating. Aggregate earnings are up just over 32% YoY versus roughly 25% projected at end of September.
Full-year S&P 500 earnings growth is expected at 30.4% in 2026, 20.4% in 2027 and 16.4% in 2028.
Initial jobless claims rose 1,000 to 203,000, above the 198,000 consensus. October retail sales rose 0.2% after a 0.8% gain in September.
Week ahead: October PCE, personal income and spending, durable goods and new home sales on Wednesday, plus the Beige Book. Markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving and at 1 p.m. ET Friday.

market_movers.rationale: Strong quarterly results and guidance did little to renew AI optimism as the sector sold off.

sector_views.rationale: Weakest S&P sector at -12.2% for the week amid AI trade concerns, though Q3 earnings growth ranked second among sectors.

earnings_insights: Q3 S&P 500 reported through 11/20: 468 companies, over 84% beat expectations, aggregate earnings growth just over 32% YoY (reported), versus roughly 25% projected at end of September.
Nine of 11 sectors beat. Healthcare and utilities had the biggest upside surprises. Energy had the strongest YoY growth, followed by technology and industrials.
Full-year S&P 500 earnings growth expectations (forecast): 30.4% in 2026, 20.4% in 2027, 16.4% in 2028.
Upcoming reports this week (about a dozen S&P members): Dell Technologies, Analog Devices, Workday and Deere.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Slightly above the 198,000 consensus but well below 222,000 a year earlier, so the labor market remains tight.
Actual print came in modestly above expectations.
Moderated as big-ticket items like cars fell, while demand for other goods stayed resilient.
Focal data point for the week, given hawkish Fed talk about a possible December hike of 25bp or more.

macro_indicators.reading: hike possible, 25bp base case with 50bp discussed
macro_indicators.interpretation: Waller and Goolsbee float larger hikes while Williams pushes back.

risk_factors: Further Fed tightening, including a possible 50bp hike in December.
AI buildout adding inflationary pressure and concentration risk if returns disappoint.
Persistent inflation, with a risk that 3% becomes the perceived norm.
vol_and_positioning: Seven straight down sessions in the S&P 500 and a global selloff with all 11 sectors lower signal broad risk-off. No VIX or positioning data is provided.
geopolitical: Increased risk of US strikes on Iran weighed on sentiment.

tension_points.bull_case: Williams dismissed the need for an outsized hike, and some in the majority said market pricing for December and 2027 hikes was consistent with appropriate policy.
tension_points.bear_case: Waller and Goolsbee float a 50bp or larger hike, two minutes participants said more than 25bp could be warranted, and Musalem backs multiple hikes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Unfavorable incoming inflation data, such as the October PCE due Wednesday, would push toward a larger December hike.
